subject: How to access current Session / Context in the my package function implementation

messages.author: a59c03f035656bc1
messages.subject: How to access current Session / Context in the my package function implementation
parts:
Hi,

I have a Renjin package in which I implement my functions in Java. Is there a way for me to access current Session / Context reference inside my function?

Thanks,

Hao

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: How to access current Session / Context in the my package function implementation
parts:
Hi Max,

Renjin supports a sort of basic dependency injection for methods, see:
http://www.renjin.org/documentation/contributor-guide.html#contextual-arguments

You can get access to the current Session object by declaring your method this way:

public void myFunction(@Current Session session, String firstArgument, SEXP secondArgument) {  
   //...
}

HTH,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: How to access current Session / Context in the my package function implementation

Ah ok, glad that there is a work around. Can you file a bug any way?  @Context arguments should have the same behavior whether the binding to the method is made at compile time as the case is for builtins, or for methods bound at runtime via reflection.

Best,
Alex
